acceptance_criteria: AC-1: read docs/design/CAPABILITY_STATE_VOCABULARY_AND_PRESENTATION.md's D7 section in full (FROZEN -- PRODUCT OWNER APPROVED): 'D7 describes authorization and nothing else... A bearer-token session gate... keep their full enforcement power; they simply are not D7' and its historical note about a prior overreach that folded taxonomy/session gates into D7. Also read utils/action_taxonomy.py (E3, the single evaluation of taxonomy admissibility -- D7/E4 never re-evaluate it) and console/app.py's existing bearer-token/loopback authentication. This design must not duplicate or re-evaluate either of those -- D7 is specifically actor authorization (is THIS actor permitted THIS action), a layer on top of, not a replacement for, taxonomy admissibility and the existing session gate.

AC-2: produce a DRAFT design document (docs/design/M14_LOCAL_LDAP_AUTHORIZATION_ARCHITECTURE.md, status DRAFT -- discussion proposal, following the same document shape as docs/history/phase/OP_1_FAILOVER_PLAN_COMPILER_AND_DRY_RUN.md and docs/design/PRIVATE_REPLAY_ARCHITECTURE.md) proposing a D7 authorization producer that authenticates via a local LDAP bind against the operator's existing corporate Active Directory Domain Controller and authorizes via AD group membership -- explicitly decoupled from DEPLOY.1A (server/OIDC/RBAC track): this is a local-operator, loopback-console-scoped design, not a multi-tenant server design, and must say so explicitly rather than silently inheriting DEPLOY.1A's assumptions.

AC-3: the design must resolve, as real decisions with stated tradeoffs (not left as open questions for a second round): (a) LDAP bind credential sourcing -- reuse the existing DEV.2.1/DEV.2.2 env-var/`<VAR>_FILE`-mount pattern (application/services.py::_resolve_or_prompt/_build_runtime_config) rather than inventing a second credential path; never a credential in a config file committed to the repo, never in a URL, never in an argv the console/orchestrator would log. (b) fail-open vs fail-closed when the DC is unreachable or the bind fails -- default recommendation and why. (c) what this design can do with NO database available today: what group-membership/session state, if any, needs to persist across requests (in-memory only for the life of the console process? a short-TTL cache? never persisted at all, re-checked per request?) -- explicitly separate 'what works today, filesystem/memory only' from 'what a future DB would additionally enable (e.g. an encrypted persistent group-membership cache with a longer TTL, audit history)' as a clearly labeled later amendment, not something this draft assumes exists. (d) group-to-permission mapping model -- one group gates console access entirely, or does D7 need per-action granularity (per the frozen contract's own action-scoped E4 outcomes: NO_APPLICABLE_AUTHORITY / PERMITTED / DENIED(authority, reason) / AUTHZ_NOT_EVALUATED(authority))? State which this design targets first and why. (e) library/dependency choice for the LDAP bind (e.g. ldap3 vs python-ldap) -- state the tradeoff (pure-Python vs libldap binding, Windows/macOS/Linux portability given this runs on the operator's own machine, not just a Linux server) and a recommendation; this is a new third-party dependency, unlike the orchestrator/dashboard's own stdlib-only precedent, so justify it explicitly rather than silently assuming it's fine.

AC-4: explicitly scope what this draft does NOT decide or authorize: no code changes in this movement; no live LDAP/AD network call; this document alone does not authorize dispatch of an implementation movement (mirrors PRIVATE_REPLAY_ARCHITECTURE.md's and OP.1's own 'DRAFT, not approved' framing). Name the smallest first implementation slice (e.g. 'bind + single-group check, console-login-gating only, no per-action granularity yet') as a clearly separated, later-authorized next step, distinct from the fuller D7/per-action model this design should still describe as the eventual target.

AC-5: reconcile with the existing console authentication (console/app.py's bearer-token/session model, CON.0/CON.1) -- this LDAP-based D7 producer is an ADDITIONAL authorization layer answering 'is this authenticated actor in an authorized group', not a replacement for the existing session-token mechanism, which stays exactly as it is.

AC-6: no implementation, no test changes, no project-state file changes beyond adding this document and (if warranted) a short project/backlog.json note pointing to it -- this is a design-only movement, same validation floor as the OP.1 contract-draft and Private-Replay-draft movements before it (git diff --check, repository privacy gate, no code/test touched).

baseline.authority: This movement's own authority is entirely what it produces -- there is no existing frozen contract for local-LDAP D7 authorization to implement against. docs/design/CAPABILITY_STATE_VOCABULARY_AND_PRESENTATION.md's D7 section (FROZEN) is the one constraint this draft must not violate: D7 is authorization only, never re-evaluates taxonomy admissibility (E3) or the existing session gate.
baseline.sequencing: Independent of every other in-flight movement -- new document only, no shared file surface. Product Owner direction 2026-09-08: this decouples M14 from its previous (incorrect) DEPLOY.1A dependency -- M14 was blocked in project state pending server infrastructure that this local-LDAP approach does not need. Not urgent to implement today (the Product Owner is currently fine using their own credentials manually); this movement is architecture-only, to have a resolved design ready before implementation is prioritized.
